sections.strategic_report: STRATEGIC REPORT (CONTINUED) FOR THE PERIOD ENDED 31 JULY 2024 - 2 - Financial and sustainability Significant upfront investment in infrastructure and services has created a strong foundation for growth: The group is outperforming national market share growth in Scotland at twice the average rate. Private services revenues are increasing, reinforcing resilience beyond NHS funding. Trading has been impacted by NHS underpayments, recognised outside trading reports but expected to be recovered. In the first twelve months, performance was also affected by one-off, non-recurring items: Remittances for stock purchased by the former owner under the transitional services agreement, not disclosed until after completion. Estimated NHS payments in place of actual reconciliations for the first six months of trading. These items have been treated transparently to provide a clear picture of underlying performance. Key performance indicators (KPIs) The directors monitor performance using a range of financial and operational KPIs, including: Turnover Growth – year-on-year revenue performance monitored against budget and sector benchmarks. Gross Profit Margin – tracked monthly to assess procurement efficiency, pricing strategy, and service mix sustainability. Market Share Growth – group pharmacies are expanding at approximately twice the Scottish national average. Prescription Volume – maintained strong growth, with central hub capacity to absorb up to 70% of dispensing volume. Private Service Revenues – continued increases across travel health, diagnostics, vaccinations, and testing. Patient Access Metrics – volume of online bookings and uptake of 24/7 automated collection points. Sustainability Progress – proportion of deliveries completed via the green fleet. Staff Development – number of pharmacists trained as prescribers and staff achieving technician and accuracy-checking roles. These KPIs provide a balanced assessment of financial performance, operational efficiency, patient access, and workforce development. Risk management The group operates in a complex regulatory and commercial environment. The directors have identified the following key risks and mitigation strategies: NHS Funding Risk – ongoing underfunding and delayed payments impact cashflow. Mitigation: diversification into private services, advance payment models, and financial reserves. Supply Chain Risk – shortages and pricing volatility. Mitigation: central warehouse redistribution, bulk purchasing, and wholesaler partnerships. Regulatory Risk – evolving healthcare regulation. Mitigation: compliance teams, training, and prescriber qualifications. Technology & Cyber Risk – reliance on digital systems. Mitigation: secure IT infrastructure, audits, and data protection. Workforce Recruitment & Retention – shortage of pharmacists. Mitigation: career pathways, training investment, competitive packages. Reputation & Patient Trust – service failures or supply interruptions. Mitigation: robust governance, patient engagement, transparent communication. AMIRY & GILBRIDE HEALTHCARE LIMITED
